## Plan: PttChrome Security and Release Roadmap

This plan turns the supplied dev-branch recommendations into a four-milestone implementation roadmap. It starts at the terminal/preview trust boundary, then stabilizes connection and persistence ownership, adds bounded parser/resource behavior and end-to-end coverage, and finishes with CI, deployment traceability, and release documentation. The current GitHub Pages deployment shape remains in place, and credentials remain terminal-only and non-persistent.

**Steps**

### Phase 0 - Baseline and guardrails
1. Record the current verification baseline with `corepack yarn typecheck`, `corepack yarn test`, and `corepack yarn build`; preserve unrelated worktree changes.
2. Create the security and architecture decision records before implementation: trusted code/deployment origin, untrusted BBS text, external URLs/images, browser storage, WebSocket/proxy, Telnet versus SSH, credentials, and GitHub Pages supply chain.
3. Establish the ownership map: `TermBuf` owns terminal contents/cursor, the connection/session layer owns lifecycle and session identity, `usePreferencesStore` owns non-sensitive settings, the context-menu store or local React state owns dialogs, preview components own preview state, and no store owns DOM nodes or credentials. This baseline blocks all later phases.

### Phase 1 - P0 security gate
4. Audit every terminal-to-DOM path, including `src/js/term_ui.js`, `src/js/term_view.js`, `src/js/easy_reading.js`, `src/components/Screen.tsx`, `src/components/Row/`, `WordSegmentBuilder/`, alerts, and helper dialogs. Keep static UI markup only where its source is fixed; render terminal-derived content as text/React nodes, map ANSI state to finite internal classes, and remove or isolate any terminal-derived HTML parsing sink. Add regression tests for HTML-like text, malformed URLs, and event-handler attributes.
5. Make one URL policy the only boundary for external navigation and preview. Extend the existing `getSafeExternalUrl`/`openExternalUrl` boundary in `src/js/util.js` with a typed valid/invalid result or a typed compatibility wrapper, using the standard `URL` API, rejecting whitespace-obfuscated schemes, credentials, malformed hosts/ports, fragments where policy disallows them, and unsupported protocols. Preserve only explicitly required navigation schemes; require `https:` for image-preview output unless a documented provider exception exists. Keep `HyperLink.tsx` as a second render-time check and keep `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on new-tab links.
6. Harden `src/components/ImagePreviewer.resolvers.ts`, `ImagePreviewer.core.tsx`, and `ImagePreviewer.types.ts`. Validate the original URL, validate every provider-rewritten URL again, keep displayed link text separate from navigation URLs, bound URL length and pending preview work, cancel or invalidate stale fetch/image work when the target changes, and add an intentional image `referrerPolicy`. Do not ship the client-visible Flickr API key: remove the Flickr resolver for this release or replace it with a server-side endpoint whose contract and secret handling are separately specified. Preserve the existing `enablePicPreview` behavior; do not add automatic credential or image-preview persistence.
7. Expand `HyperLink.test.tsx` and `ImagePreviewer.test.tsx` with the supplied adversarial corpus: `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, embedded credentials, lookalike Imgur hosts, encoded nulls, protocol-relative URLs, nested redirect parameters, unsupported schemes, and malicious provider output. Assert that invalid input produces a typed rejection/fallback rather than a partly sanitized URL.
8. Replace naive connection destination parsing in `src/js/main.tsx`, `src/js/runtime_env.js`, and `App.prototype._parseURLSimple`/`_setupWebsocketConn` in `src/js/pttchrome.js` with one explicit policy. Validate scheme mapping (`wstelnet`/`wsstelnet` and any retained Telnet/SSH adapters), hostname, port, path, credentials, and fragments; prefer secure WebSocket destinations for deployed builds; keep `ALLOW_SITE_IN_QUERY` opt-in and validate query overrides before use. Do not add a persisted proxy-URL setting, and do not allow BBS content or worker messages to select a destination.
9. Inventory the production bundle in `index.html`, `vite.config.mts`, React style usage, dynamic styles in `term_view.js`, worker/connect code, fonts, and preview origins. Add the strongest hosting-compatible CSP, avoiding `unsafe-eval` and minimizing `unsafe-inline`; for GitHub Pages, document the limits of meta-delivered CSP versus response headers. Run the production bundle with the policy enabled and fix unexpected violations rather than broadening directives blindly.
10. Add `SECURITY.md` with supported branches/releases, private reporting instructions, requested reproduction data, credential-exposure handling, and scope covering the browser client, WebSocket worker/proxy, and Pages deployment. Update `README.md` with the no-credential-persistence decision, Telnet/SSH limitations, third-party image-preview privacy, supported browsers, local commands, deployment model, and branch/release behavior. Phase 1 is complete only when terminal data cannot reach an HTML parsing sink, preview output is strictly validated, destinations are constrained, and the production smoke test is clean.

### Phase 2 - P0 architectural stabilization
11. Introduce a typed connection state model in `src/types/connection.ts` and make `useAppRuntimeStore` expose centralized transitions instead of inferring lifecycle from numeric state and alert combinations. Use `idle`, `connecting`, `authenticating` when applicable, `connected`, `disconnecting`, `disconnected`, and `failed`; retain a compatibility mapping only where the legacy core still requires it.
12. Add a session identifier at `App.connect`/`_attachConn` time. Capture it in every WebSocket/Telnet callback, ignore events from inactive connections, make close/error handling idempotent, wire the existing `Websocket._onError` event into `App`, and dispose timers/subscriptions during teardown. Add bounded, user-cancellable reconnect attempts for unplanned close or worker restart; never create an infinite reconnect loop or reconnect after an explicit disconnect.
13. Version and validate preference persistence in `src/store/index.ts`. Replace the unversioned `{ values }` payload with a versioned `PersistedPreferences` envelope, parse safely, validate each field and nested `termSize` range, migrate known versions, reject unknown/corrupt shapes to defaults, and avoid merging arbitrary persisted objects into live state. Extend `src/store/index.test.ts` for old versions, invalid types/ranges, unknown versions, reset behavior, and storage failures. Follow the settings-flow instruction if any setting surface changes.
14. Complete subsystem migrations vertically, in this order: URL/preview, preferences/persistence, connection and worker messages, parser/buffer, row rendering, then helpers/dialogs. For each slice, finish types, runtime validation, tests, ownership notes, and removal of superseded adapters before starting the next. Do not perform a broad legacy `src/js/` rewrite, persist terminal buffers, or add autologin fields.

### Phase 3 - P1 parser and resource quality
15. Define centralized limits for terminal rows/columns, scrollback, escape and OSC/control-string length, incoming WebSocket payloads, URL length, input-helper insertion, preview concurrency, alert queue size, and reconnect attempts. Enforce them at `src/js/term_buf.js`, `src/js/ansi_parser.js`, `src/js/websocket.ts`, input-helper code, preview resolvers, and connection lifecycle boundaries. Clamp cursor/resize operations and reset decoder/parser state when a session changes.
16. Add parser and encoding tests for fragmented Big5 and UTF-8 data, split escape sequences, malformed bytes, huge cursor coordinates, unsupported CSI/OSC commands, resize during input, repeated cursor movement/backspace, combining and wide characters, decoder state across reconnect, and reset behavior. Add property-style deterministic generators/corpus checks for bounded output, in-range cursor state, no uncaught parser exceptions, and no executable markup in rendered output.
17. Add a deterministic mock transport/BBS integration harness that emits login screens, fragmented ANSI data, malformed controls, URLs/image links, disconnects/reconnects, delayed events, and oversized rows. Exercise mock transport through decoder, parser, buffer, React bridge, and DOM; verify stale session events cannot mutate the new screen. Keep browser production smoke coverage separate from jsdom integration coverage.

### Phase 4 - P1 CI, deployment, and release quality
18. Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml` into mandatory merge checks for immutable install, typecheck, lint, unit/security regression tests, terminal integration tests, production build, and dependency review/audit. Add the smallest lint configuration that covers typed/React code first and stages legacy JavaScript separately; do not use linting as a reason to opportunistically rewrite the terminal core. Keep top-level permissions read-only, retain pinned action SHAs, add job timeouts, and avoid exposing secrets or running privileged deployment work on pull-request content.
19. Preserve the current `.github/workflows/pages.yml` branch/default-branch behavior and protected `github-pages` environment. Ensure pull requests build and test without deploying, the Pages job remains limited to the intended repository owner/default ref, and the production smoke check runs against the built artifact before release. Document the current `dev`/default-branch behavior rather than introducing a new deployment model.
20. Make builds traceable. Add version, commit SHA, and CI build date through `vite.config.mts` and `src/js/runtime_env.js`, expose them through the existing developer/diagnostic surface or a stable build-info asset, and ensure the metadata is derived from immutable build inputs rather than runtime storage. Add `CHANGELOG.md` and a release checklist covering exact tags, security-relevant changes, supported browsers, transport limitations, reproducible inputs, and known credential/privacy behavior.
21. Verify licensing and attribution before release: confirm `LICENSE` and SPDX expression, upstream notices, bundled font/icon/image licenses, dependency licenses, and source availability for distributed builds. Add a third-party notices document only where the audit finds obligations that are not already represented.

**Relevant files**
- `src/components/Row/HyperLink.tsx`, `src/components/Row/LinkSegmentBuilder.tsx`, `src/components/Row/ColorSegmentBuilder.ts`, `src/components/Screen.tsx` - terminal text, ANSI classes, link rendering, and preview entry points.
- `src/components/ImagePreviewer.resolvers.ts`, `src/components/ImagePreviewer.core.tsx`, `src/components/ImagePreviewer.types.ts`, `src/components/ImagePreviewer.test.tsx` - provider rewriting, image loading/cancellation, render state, and preview security tests.
- `src/js/util.js`, `src/js/term_buf.js`, `src/js/term_ui.js`, `src/js/term_view.js`, `src/js/easy_reading.js`, `src/js/ansi_parser.js` - URL policy compatibility, URI detection, terminal-to-DOM bridge, legacy markup, parser, and resource limits.
- `src/js/main.tsx`, `src/js/runtime_env.js`, `src/js/pttchrome.js`, `src/js/websocket.ts`, `src/js/telnet.ts`, `src/types/connection.ts` - bootstrap destination selection, connection parsing, lifecycle events, transport boundaries, and typed state/session identity.
- `src/store/index.ts`, `src/store/index.test.ts`, `src/components/ContextMenu/PrefModal.js` - preference schema, persistence/migrations, runtime ownership, and settings flow.
- `src/components/AppAlertHost.js`, `src/components/ConnectionAlert.js`, `src/components/DeveloperModeAlert.js`, `src/js/en_US_messages.js`, `src/js/zh_TW_messages.js` - connection/error/reconnect UI and localized strings if new user-visible states are added.
- `vite.config.mts`, `index.html`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/pages.yml` - CSP/runtime inventory, scripts, type coverage, CI gates, and current Pages deployment.
- `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/threat-model.md`, `docs/state-ownership.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, and any generated third-party notices - governance, architecture, release, and attribution documentation.

**Verification**
1. Before implementation, capture the existing `corepack yarn typecheck`, `corepack yarn test`, and `corepack yarn build` results.
2. After Phase 1, run focused URL/preview and DOM-rendering tests, scan the built source for HTML parsing sinks and bundled secrets, build with CSP enabled, and use `corepack yarn preview --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4173` for a production smoke test. Exercise safe links, unsafe schemes, provider rewrites, image failures, stale hover targets, and keyboard/focus behavior.
3. After Phase 2, test every connection transition, error-before-close, explicit disconnect, bounded reconnect, worker restart, stale event, rapid connect/disconnect, preference migration, corrupt storage, and session reset. Confirm no credentials or terminal contents are written to storage or logs.
4. After Phase 3, run the deterministic parser corpus and mock BBS integration suite, including fragmented encodings, malformed controls, oversized inputs, reconnects, and DOM assertions. Check invariants for bounded output, valid cursor coordinates, no uncaught exceptions, and no executable markup.
5. After Phase 4, require `corepack yarn install --immutable`, `corepack yarn typecheck`, `corepack yarn lint`, `corepack yarn test`, the security/dependency audit, and `corepack yarn build` in CI. Confirm pull requests cannot deploy Pages, action references remain immutable, permissions are least-privilege, and build metadata identifies the exact commit.
6. Use a final manual release checklist: inspect CSP console output, image/network destinations, Telnet/SSH warning text, credential-storage documentation, Pages deployment source, generated build metadata, license/asset attribution, and `CHANGELOG.md` before tagging.

**Decisions**
- Scope is the full four-milestone roadmap, sequenced with the terminal renderer and URL/image-preview subsystem as the first implementation gate.
- GitHub Pages deployment behavior stays in place; hardening is added around the existing default-branch/protected-environment flow rather than moving production to a new release ref in this roadmap.
- Credentials remain terminal-only. Do not add username/password preferences, autologin, session-storage workarounds, or credential-bearing URLs/logs/devtools.
- Do not add a persisted proxy destination setting. Query overrides remain opt-in and must pass the same destination validator as defaults.
- Do not persist terminal buffers or replay session input. Session identity protects asynchronous state, while terminal contents remain in memory.
- Do not ship a browser-bundled provider secret. Flickr support is removed until a server-side contract exists, or it is changed to use an approved server-side proxy as a separately reviewed work item.
- Preserve existing inline preview behavior behind `enablePicPreview`; document third-party image requests and enforce strict validated HTTPS output instead of adding a new interaction gate in this roadmap.
- Legacy `src/js/` remains function-constructor/prototype/jQuery code unless a narrow security or lifecycle boundary requires a change; no percentage-driven rewrite is included.

**Dependencies and scope boundaries**
- Phase 0 blocks all implementation. Steps 4-7 can proceed in parallel with steps 8-10 after the policy decisions are recorded; their integration tests and CSP smoke test are the Phase 1 gate.
- Steps 11-14 depend on the Phase 1 URL/destination policy. Preference migration and connection state work can proceed in parallel, but both must finish before the end-to-end harness.
- Steps 15-17 depend on the ownership/session model and feed Phase 4 test and CI gates.
- Steps 18-21 depend on the tests and policies being stable; release tagging is the final action, after CI and manual verification pass.
- Explicitly excluded: a new server/proxy implementation in this repository, autologin, credential storage, terminal-buffer persistence, a full JavaScript-to-TypeScript rewrite, unrelated UI redesign, and changing Pages from its current deployment model.
